strengths: Well-motivated problem: Addresses a genuine limitation in existing text-to-video models regarding extreme camera angles (top-down, Dutch angles, 360° pans) using gravity as an intuitive global reference.

Clever data augmentation pipeline: The extraction of camera poses from 360° panoramic videos combined with on-the-fly random trajectory sampling effectively covers the full sphere of camera orientations, including rare cinematic shots absent from natural video distributions.

Practical null-pitch conditioning strategy: The observation that models overemphasize prompts when camera angles conflict with text is insightful. Captioning forward-looking crops is simple yet effective, showing 67% improvement in pitch error when ablated.

Comprehensive evaluation framework: Two new benchmarks (SpatialVID-extreme and entanglement benchmark) are valuable community contributions. The prompt-camera entanglement evaluation is particularly novel and well-designed.
Strong empirical results on camera metrics: Substantial improvements over baselines on PitchErr (9.35° vs 16.25° for UCPE), GravityErr, and RotErr demonstrate effective camera control.
Clear presentation: The paper is well-written with informative figures effectively illustrating the methodology and results, particularly Figures 3 and 5.
weaknesses: Limited technical/algorithmic novelty: The core contribution is a data augmentation strategy and simple null-pitch conditioning—not a novel architectural or algorithmic advance. The camera encoder is minimal (two convolution layers), and the method builds entirely on an existing pretrained model (WAN-2.2) with only 30k iterations of fine-tuning.

Scope limitation—no new camera translations: The method only controls rotations (pitch/roll) at extreme angles. Translations are constrained to those in source videos. This significantly limits cinematic expressivity and reduces the 'control' narrative, as acknowledged in limitations but understated in claims.

Serious benchmark methodology concerns: (1) SpatialVID-extreme artificially adds roll by video warping—synthetic data that may not reflect real challenges; (2) Only 140 videos with manually filtered pitch distribution; (3) Entanglement benchmark is small (20 scenes × 19 angles = 380 samples); (4) Ground-truth camera angles rely on Perspective Fields [19], a learned model whose accuracy is not validated; roll error is 'unreliable near poles,' leaving a critical evaluation blind spot.

Substantial data filtering (38% discarded) introduces unknown biases: Videos discarded for pose estimation failure or 'extreme acceleration' raises reproducibility and generalization concerns. No analysis of which scene types or camera motion patterns are systematically excluded.

Marginal improvements over concurrent work: UCPE [50] achieves 16.25° PitchErr vs. 9.35° for this work, but the difference is modest given UCPE's simpler approach. CLIP scores are lower (20.63 vs. 22.50), and FID is higher (115.58 vs. 110.66), suggesting visual quality trade-offs are not favorable. The novelty advantage over UCPE is incremental.

Visual quality degradation not adequately addressed: Lower CLIP scores, higher FID, and acknowledged artifacts (e.g., 'faceless man' in Fig. 5) indicate quality trade-offs. No systematic analysis of when/why visual fidelity is compromised for camera control.

Limited and unfair baseline comparisons: (1) Most baselines (PreciseCam+GEN3C) are designed for static scenes and thus not comparable on dynamic video metrics; (2) AC3D variants are not well-suited for absolute camera control; (3) Panorama generation methods (360dvd, PanoWAN) discussed but not compared; (4) Comparison with UCPE—claimed inability to handle extremes (Fig. 2)—seems cherry-picked; no systematic analysis of relative strengths.

Insufficient evaluation of camera accuracy mechanisms: Multiple dependencies on external models (ViPE [17] for pose, Perspective Fields [19] for gravity, InternVL [52] for captioning) create potential error propagation. Accuracy of ground-truth pose/gravity estimation is not validated. Gravity estimation uses 8 perspective crops—no ablation on this choice.

Reproducibility and generalization concerns: (1) Heavy reliance on multiple external components; (2) Many implementation details deferred to supplementary material; (3) No code availability mentioned; (4) Training only on PanoVid YouTube videos with no zero-shot generalization testing; (5) Unclear dataset release scope despite promises.

Incomplete ablation studies: Only null-pitch conditioning is ablated. Missing ablations on: camera encoder architecture, zero-initialization strategy, spatial bias toward poles (acknowledged but not studied), and sensitivity to hyperparameters (learning rate, training iterations, FoV range).

Problematic evaluation of prompt-camera entanglement: CLIP score comparison (Section 4.6) is confounded—lower prompts scores expected when camera contradicts text, making direct comparison uninformative. The proposed 'ground-truth frame CLIP' workaround is reasonable but small-scale.

Contribution type mismatch: The paper is primarily a dataset/benchmark + applied systems contribution (data augmentation), not an algorithmic advance. Evaluated as an algorithms paper, the novelty is thin. Even as a dataset paper, benchmarks are small and partially synthetic.

strengths: Clear problem formulation: Extreme camera control (pitch, roll, extreme rotations) in text-to-video generation is a genuine limitation of existing methods, and the paper articulates this well.

Sensible use of 360° video data: Leveraging panoramic videos to generate training data covering the full sphere of viewpoints is a practical solution to the out-of-distribution problem for extreme angles.

Comprehensive experimental validation: The paper includes multiple metrics (geometry-specific: PitchErr, GravityErr, RotErr; quality: FID, FVD, CLIP), strong ablations showing null-pitch conditioning provides 35-72% pitch error reduction, and comparisons across multiple backbones and conditioning mechanisms.
Null-pitch conditioning insight: The observation that captioning at pitch/roll=0° reduces entanglement between text and camera angle is intuitive and empirically validated.
New evaluation benchmarks: Two benchmarks for extreme camera control and prompt-camera entanglement are useful contributions, addressing evaluation gaps in the literature.
Architecture-agnostic approach: Demonstrates applicability across CogVideoX and WAN models with both UCPE and Plücker conditioning.
Well-motivated design choices: The gravity-aligned coordinate system is more interpretable than relative encodings, and the random trajectory sampling strategy is clearly motivated.
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Core contributions are incremental combinations of existing techniques—360° video augmentation, standard SfM, straightforward random trajectory sampling (Algorithm 1), and simple data processing (null-pitch conditioning). The model training is standard diffusion finetuning with no novel architectural or algorithmic components.

Unclear technical details on gravity alignment: Equations 4 and supporting methodology (φ(·) and ψ(·)) are incompletely explained in the main paper. Robustness of gravity estimation from 360° videos is not analyzed. High filtering rate (38% of videos discarded) raises questions about dataset bias, but impacts are not discussed.

Translation augmentation fundamentally limited: Authors acknowledge inability to augment camera translations, restricting to only original translations. This is a significant limitation mentioned only briefly, with vague future work on 3DGS but no preliminary results or solutions presented.

Marginal video quality improvements: FID and FVD scores show the method is competitive but not clearly superior to baselines. CLIP scores slightly decrease. Visual artifacts acknowledged (e.g., 'distortions in Tokyo Skytree') but not systematically analyzed. Trade-offs between camera control and visual quality are inadequately explored.

Small-scale benchmarks with methodological concerns: SpatialVID-extreme contains only 138 videos with manually filtered pitch distribution. Roll angles are artificially added via warping—not realistic physics-based augmentation. Prompt-entanglement benchmark uses only 20 panoramas (380 test pairs), too limited for robust evaluation. No discussion of validation/test splits.

Questionable entanglement metric validity: The CLIP-to-ground-truth metric (Fig. 6b, bottom) shows only modest improvements and is an indirect measure. No direct validation that the model truly follows camera conditioning over prompt conflation. Theoretical justification for why null-pitch conditioning specifically solves entanglement is lacking.

Insufficient reproducibility: Dataset preparation details sparse, hyperparameters scattered across supplementary material, VLM captioning procedure unclear, and no mention of code or model release. Camera encoder architecture for WAN-2.2 is mentioned as 'smaller' without specifications.

Incomplete failure analysis: Systematic analysis of failure modes is absent. Which camera angles remain difficult? When does gravity estimation fail? How do filtering and preprocessing biases manifest in generations? Visual artifacts are acknowledged but not characterized.

Unfair or incomplete baseline comparisons: UCPE is concurrent work, complicating temporal comparison. GEN3C cannot handle dynamic scenes, limiting its relevance. Ablation for AC3D's text-based absolute pitch/roll inclusion is undocumented. Why some baselines perform poorly is unclear.

Null-pitch conditioning lacks theoretical grounding: While empirically effective, the mechanism is not deeply understood. Why does forward-facing captioning generalize to extreme angles? Is this solution architecture-specific or fundamental? Ablations show the effect but not the 'why'.
